_comment: Cited eligibility limits per authority (#679): a utility's customer-generation program or an AHJ's simplified permit path. Loaded by backend/src/eligibilityLimits.ts and seeded into authority_eligibility_limits; a verified row is never overwritten (rule 3). Every limit carries its source by name, URL and verbatim words.

records.programName: Idaho Power on-site generation (residential Schedule 1 / small general service Schedule 7)

maxAcKw.appliesOnlyTo: residential (Schedule 1) and small general service (Schedule 7) customers; inverter AC nameplate, energy storage not counted
maxAcKw.message: AC size is {value} kW{combinedNote}. Idaho Power caps residential and small general service generation at {limit} kW AC (inverter nameplate; storage not counted). Confirm before filing.

citation.sourceName: Idaho Power — Customer generation frequently asked questions
citation.quote: Idaho and Oregon residential (Schedule 1) and small general service (Schedule 7) customers may connect energy generation sources (e.g. solar) with a total nameplate capacity of 25 kilowatts (kW) AC or less.

maxDcKw.appliesOnlyTo: residential customer-generators of a public utility
maxDcKw.message: DC size is {value} kW{combinedNote}. Confirm this is not a {program} capped at {limit} kW.

citation.quote: For residential customer-generators of a public utility, these rules apply to net metering facilities that have a generating capacity of 25 kilowatts or less.
